title: Space bound for compiled nondeterministic programs
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with initial label $l_0$, oracle, and decider machine $D$ with initial states $q_0$, and let $B,W,N$ be natural numbers. Suppose every sequence of $N$ choice bits makes the program halt, and each configuration before halting satisfies the guard: its applicable instruction preconditions hold, every decider call has distinct argument registers and a clean run using at most $B$ work-head cells, and each register value $z$ satisfies $|\text{the binary length of }z+1|\le W$. Then there is a number $T$ such that the compiled machine halts for every length-$T$ choice sequence and uses at most $m(W+2)+k_D(2B+1)$ work-tape cells on each such run. Moreover, there exists a length-$N$ choice sequence on which the register program's answer is true if and only if the compiled machine has an accepting run of length $T$.
